title: Cloning and Functional Characterization of Lj3GT, a Flavonoid 3-O-Glycosyltransferase Involved in Anthocyanidin Glycosylation in Lonicera japonica Thunb. var. chinensis (Wats.) Bak.
content: Red honeysuckle (Lonicera japonica var. chinensis) is valued for its red flowers, whose colour is largely determined by anthocyanins decorated by flavonoid 3-O-glycosyltransferases (3GTs). To clarify the molecular basis of flower colour formation in this variety, the 3GT gene Lj3GT was cloned from petals and characterised at the sequence, expression and enzymatic levels. The 1335 bp coding sequence encodes a 445-amino-acid hydrophilic protein predicted to be cytosolic; AlphaFold 2 modelling revealed a monomeric protein with the canonical GT-B fold, and phylogenetic analysis placed Lj3GT within the 3-O-glycosyltransferase clade. Lj3GT was expressed in all tissues, and its transcript abundance followed a rise-and-fall pattern during flower development. Recombinant expression was optimised in Escherichia coli: the pCold I vector combined with BL21(DE3)/pG-Tf2 chaperone co-expression achieved high-level soluble production, and the Ni-NTA-purified enzyme (>95% purity) was characterised. Lj3GT glycosylated both cyanidin and pelargonidin following Michaelis–Menten kinetics (R² = 0.98–0.99), with Km values of 145.70 and 264.34 μmol/L and kcat values of 12.04 and 13.43 s⁻¹, respectively. The ~1.6-fold higher catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) toward cyanidin was imposed at the substrate-binding step, providing a mechanistic basis for the anthocyanin composition of red honeysuckle.
